config.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday

personas.name: Noor
personas.goals: A clear record and practical fixes
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to make fallback paths a standard for every vendor

personas.name: Samuel
personas.hidden_agenda: Wasn't sure he was allowed to switch the fraud check off

personas.name: Lin
personas.role: Payments engineer, owns the fraud-check integration
personas.hidden_agenda: Wrote the original integration three years ago

personas.name: Abby
personas.hidden_agenda: Her team found out from customers before engineering told them

agenda.title: Cause
agenda.goal: Understand why a slow vendor took checkout down

agenda.title: Impact
agenda.goal: Size the effect on customers and revenue

facts.statement: Fraud API p99 latency during the incident = 12 seconds
Vendor incidents affecting us this year = 2

beats.summary: Start, detection and end; Samuel overstates the duration
Why a slow vendor stopped checkout; Lin's timeout figure stays wrong
Orders, money and tickets; Abby's ticket count corrected later
Owners and dates; one item without an owner

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Thanks, everyone. This is a blameless review. Samuel, could you take us through Tuesday afternoon?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: Sure. Checkout errors started at about a quarter past three.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: How quickly did we notice?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: The alert fired four minutes in. That part worked well.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Our chat queue lit up at about the same time, for what it's worth.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Did anyone tell support at that point?

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: And how long were we down altogether?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: About an hour, I'd say. It felt like a long afternoon.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: The incident record has thirty-eight minutes, from first error to recovery.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: Thirty-eight. That's right. The hour includes the time we spent watching it afterwards.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: What ended it?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: The vendor's latency came back down on its own. We didn't actually fix anything.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Which is the uncomfortable part. We were waiting on them.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Did anyone consider switching the fraud check off?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: I thought about it. I wasn't sure I was allowed to. There's no runbook entry for it.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: That's a gap in the runbook, not on you, Samuel.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: The cause. Lin, you know the integration best.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: The fraud-check vendor got slow. Their p99 latency went up to twelve seconds.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Twelve seconds per check?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Per check. And our timeout is ten seconds, so most calls timed out and the order failed.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Why does a timeout fail the order, rather than letting it through?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: When I built it, the rule was "if in doubt, block". We never revisited it.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: So a slow vendor looks the same as a fraudulent order.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Exactly that. What does the vendor promise us?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Ninety-nine point nine percent uptime. They'd argue they were up, just slow.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Has this happened before with them?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Twice this year now. The first one was short enough that nobody noticed.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: The weather station in my village says it's going to snow on Friday, by the way. In April.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: My tulips are going to be furious.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Let's come back to the cause. Lin, what would a safer default look like?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Let small orders through when the check times out, and hold large orders for manual review.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Is there a threshold that makes sense?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Most fraud we see is over a hundred and fifty dollars. Under that, letting it through is low risk.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Then let's adopt that: on a timeout, orders under a hundred and fifty go through, and larger ones are held for review.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: I'll build the fallback and have it in review by next Thursday.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Impact. How many orders failed?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Twelve hundred and forty failed. But eight hundred and seventy were retried automatically and went through later.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: So the real loss is smaller than the first number.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: And the revenue impact?

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Finance estimates forty-one thousand, before the retries are counted.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: We had about five hundred support tickets. People were very worried their cards had been charged.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Were they charged?

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: No. A failed fraud check means no charge was made.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: That's good to know. Our macros didn't say that clearly.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: Could support get a short statement for this kind of failure, so they're not guessing?

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Yes, please. I'll write a draft macro and send it to Lin to check.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: Happy to check it.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Sorry, correcting myself, the ticket report says three hundred and ten, not five hundred. Five hundred was all contacts, including chat.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Actions. We have the fallback from Lin and the macro from Abby.

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: And a runbook entry for switching the fraud check off. So the next person knows they can.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Samuel, would you write that entry, since you were there?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: Yes. I'll write the runbook entry this week.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Should we ask the vendor for a service credit? Their SLA is about uptime, but it's worth asking.

turns.speaker: Lin
turns.text: They've already offered five thousand. It came in this morning.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Then we accept the credit and ask for a latency commitment in the renewal.

turns.speaker: Abby
turns.text: Who's talking to the vendor about the renewal?

turns.speaker: Samuel
turns.text: Should every vendor integration have a fallback like this one?

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: I think so. I'll raise it with the architecture group next week. Thank you, everyone. A good, honest review.
